newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end up on Dow's rise, Merrill report.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end up on Dow's rise, Merrill report.

text.p: Philippine shares closed higher on Friday on news Merrill Lynch had favoured the Philippines after underweighting Hong Kong and also because of the Dow's record finish, traders said.

"The Hong Kong market is overheated and indeed if we do see some sharp sell-off there, some funds may be coursing their way to the Philippines as part of an Asian play," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
The main index ended 13.87 points higher at 2,801.61, a notch up from the 2,800 resistance.

"We may be mimicking what's happening in New York. And what we've had from 2,500 up to this level is a normalisation of values as the recent lows were illogical and unreasonable," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities Phils Inc.
The Dow posted its fifth straight record finish on Thursday ending at 7,711.47 points.
Traders said the market's rise was led by blue chips namely PLDT and Petron Corp. But in the broader market, bears outnumbered bulls 60 to 49.

Anscor-Hagedorn Securities vice-president Noel Reyes said the market will continue its consolidation phase next week with an upward bias until the market closes convincingly beyond the 2,800 mark. The next major resistance is seen at 2,950 points, he added.
